questions_json.explanation: Herzberg's two-factor theory says hygiene factors (pay, conditions, policies) prevent dissatisfaction, while motivators (recognition, growth, achievement) create satisfaction. Fixing pay removed dissatisfaction but only motivators build real satisfaction.
options: Pay is a motivator in Herzberg's theory
Good pay prevents dissatisfaction but real satisfaction needs motivators like recognition and growth
Hygiene factors increase job satisfaction directly
questions_json.q: A company raises salaries but employees still feel unmotivated. According to Herzberg's two-factor theory, what is missing?

questions_json.explanation: Vroom's expectancy theory says motivation = expectancy × instrumentality × valence. The worker doubts her effort will lead to good performance (low expectancy), so motivation drops even though the bonus is attractive.
options: Expectancy — she doubts her effort will lead to good performance
Valence — she does not value the bonus
Instrumentality — she doubts good work will be rewarded
Equity — she thinks coworkers earn more
questions_json.q: A worker is offered a big bonus for high output but puts in little effort. She says, 'No matter how hard I try, I cannot reach that target.' Which part of Vroom's expectancy theory is low?

questions_json.explanation: Transformational leaders inspire with vision, challenge thinking, and treat people as individuals. Transactional leaders trade rewards for performance, while laissez-faire leaders avoid involvement.
questions_json.q: A manager inspires her team with a bold vision, encourages new ideas, and mentors each member personally. The team's performance soars. Which leadership style is this?

questions_json.explanation: Structured interviews with the same job-related questions for every candidate have far higher validity than unstructured chats. Cognitive ability tests are among the strongest predictors of job performance.
options: Unstructured interviews, because they feel natural
Structured interviews with the same job-related questions for every candidate
Choosing the candidate with the longest CV
questions_json.q: A company wants to improve its hiring. Which selection method has the strongest research support for predicting job performance?

questions_json.explanation: Social loafing is reduced effort when individual contributions are hidden in a group. Making each member's work visible and accountable restores effort.
questions_json.q: In a group project, some students do almost no work, assuming others will cover for them. This is an example of:

questions_json.explanation: Burnout (Maslach) has three parts: emotional exhaustion, depersonalization/cynicism, and reduced personal accomplishment. The nurse shows exhaustion and cynicism toward patients.
questions_json.q: A nurse feels emotionally drained, has become cynical toward patients, and feels she achieves nothing anymore. Which condition is this?

questions_json.explanation: Locke's goal-setting theory says specific, difficult (but reachable) goals plus feedback produce the best performance. Vague 'do your best' goals perform worse.
options: Specific, challenging goals with regular feedback
questions_json.q: A sales team performs best when given clear monthly targets that are tough but achievable, plus weekly progress updates. Which goal approach does research support?

questions_json.explanation: Adams' equity theory says people compare their input/output ratio with others'. Perceived unfairness creates tension, so people reduce effort, demand more, or leave.
questions_json.q: Two employees do the same work, but one discovers the other earns more. The lower-paid one starts arriving late and doing the minimum. Which theory explains this?

questions_json.explanation: 360-degree feedback collects ratings from supervisors, peers, subordinates, and self, giving a fuller picture than a single supervisor's view and reducing individual bias.
options: It is cheaper than supervisor ratings
It removes the need for any supervisor input
It gathers ratings from supervisors, peers, subordinates, and self for a fuller picture
It guarantees promotions for top scorers
questions_json.q: A company switches from supervisor-only reviews to 360-degree feedback. What is the main advantage of this method?

questions_json.explanation: Job satisfaction is an attitude toward one's job, predicted by the work itself, fair pay, supportive coworkers, and good supervision. It correlates with lower turnover and absenteeism.
options: The work itself, fair pay, supportive coworkers, and good supervision
Only the size of the salary
Only the length of lunch breaks
questions_json.q: Research shows job satisfaction is most strongly predicted by which set of factors?
